about: CM step 2 batch 4 (census Q12, harness gap H1): what the favorites list is after a rename or merge. Each scenario is a small graph, one operation and the proposed one answer (`target`). Three entries run every scenario and record where they differ from `target` in expected-differences.json: `rust` (tine-graph-features `pages::rename_or_merge_page`, the entry the app and the CLI owner both call), `owner` (the headless CLI owner's `page.rename` verb, src-tauri owner tests: `tine serve` has no window, so nothing in TypeScript runs after it) and `frontend` (src/favorites.ts `renameFavorite`, reached as graph.ts `refreshAfterRename` reaches it after an app rename or a CLI rename a window hears about). `target` is the manager's stated goal (favorites follow a rename; a merged-away page's favorite ends on the survivor) plus OG's namespace behaviour; `pending` names a target that is a proposal awaiting a ruling (see the design note cm-step2-favorites-design.md). Names avoid the owner test graph's seed pages (a, b, ns, ns/child, dup).

scenarios.about: A favorite page is renamed; another favorite stays.
scenarios.og: rename-page-aux: unfavorite-page! old, favorite-page! new-page-name (lower-cased, moved to the front): ["omega" "Other"]

scenarios.about: The favorite is stored under another case spelling of the renamed page.
Renaming a namespace parent moves its descendants; a favorite descendant follows too.
scenarios.og: rename-namespace-pages! calls rename-page-aux for every namespace page, so each favorite follows: ["work" "work/child"] (front-insertion order)

scenarios.about: A favorite page is merged into an existing page that is not a favorite.
scenarios.pending: FAV-MERGE: OG drops the merged-away page's favorite (merge-pages! -> delete! -> unfavorite-page!); the brief's goal moves it to the survivor, as Tine's TypeScript does today.
scenarios.og: merge-pages! does not call rename-page-aux; delete! of the source calls unfavorite-page!: ["Other"]

scenarios.about: Both the merged-away page and the survivor are favorites: one survivor favorite remains, in the survivor's place.
The favorite is stored under an alias of the renamed page. The alias stays declared in the moved file, so the stored spelling still opens the renamed page.
scenarios.pending: FAV-ALIAS: keep the stored alias spelling (it still opens the page; a rename maps page names, not aliases) or rewrite it to the new page name, as Tine's TypeScript does today (favoriteKey resolves the alias through navigationName).
scenarios.og: favorited? compares the stored name with the old page name only; an alias spelling is not matched and stays: ["Al"]

scenarios.about: A favorite with no file, only references, is renamed (the rename repoints its references).
scenarios.og: rename-page-aux requires a page entity; a referenced name is a page in OG's DB, so it follows: ["spirit"]

scenarios.about: The renamed page is both the home page and a favorite: both follow, in one config.edn write.
A favorite listed on the Favorites arrangement page is renamed: the page's link and :favorites follow.
The Favorites arrangement page itself is renamed: :tine/favorites-page follows it.
